answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy starts with an atlas: a registry where each new identity posts a refundable bond first, so mass-creating agents stops paying. Each epoch a gale of randomized challenges sweeps the network: rotating peer audits and latency probes. Agents that fail or go silent forfeit their bonds, a bounty to the exposing peers. Trust then climbs a trellis of non-kin attestations: fresh agents handle small tasks only, each verified countersignature unlocking a higher rung. An attacker must sustain thousands of costly bonds while passing every audit, erasing the sybil edge.
